name: Taupe Grey
lede: Taupe Grey is a purplish gray classed in the 1955 ISCC-NBS system, so finely matched to plain Grey that our library puts them under 1 unit of CIEDE2000 apart.

sections.title: One name among twenty for the same patch
sections.body: The 1955 ISCC-NBS system places Taupe Grey in block 233, a purplish gray, and the library also cites Wikipedia for the name, with no record in Ridgway or Maerz and Paul for this exact word [1]. Block 233 is unusually crowded: our library files at least twenty other names, from Crane to Gull Grey to Wild Iris, into the same small region, several dated by Maerz and Paul to the 1910s and 1920s [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[rocket-metallic]], [[deep-plumbago-grey]], [[dark-heliotrope-grey]] and [[battleship-grey]], at 3.2, 3.3, 2, 3.3, 5.3 and 5.4 ΔE [1]. [[slate]], [[denim]] and [[charcoal]] all turn up more often than chance in paintings that also carry this color [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive finds a close match to Taupe Grey in 462 of 23,781 paintings, about 1.9 percent, as photographed [2]. It plays a highlight slightly more often than a midtone, 50 percent against 43 percent [2]. Jerichau, Fritz Syberg and several other Danish painters use it well above the archive's average rate [2].

The earliest dated match is a 1119 Buddhist manuscript illumination, eight centuries before the ISCC-NBS classification, which only shows a similar screen color was photographed there, not that the name existed that early, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2].
